name: button
title: Button
summary: Lets people take an action, switch something on and off, go to a destination, or send or clear the form it stands in, with one tap or click — named by a label, an icon, or both.

anatomy.description: The shape that holds the content, defines the visual bounds and carries hover, focus and press. A pill with a label; with an icon alone, as wide as it is high (a circle in the default system's corner) or at the narrow or the wide width of its size.
A glyph of the system's icon set, at the leading or the trailing side of the label, or alone. Outlined when unselected, filled when selected.
The border of the outlined variant.
Gap-then-ring indicator shown for keyboard focus.

props.name: variant
props.description: Emphasis level; whether the action deletes or discards something is destructive, which every variant takes. Use one filled button per view for the main action; an icon-only text button is the quiet icon action of a toolbar or a row. A design system may add values. Default filled; a Button placed as a dialog's or a side sheet's action without a variant takes that host's (DLG-20, SSH-17), and a side sheet's close button takes comp.side-sheet.close-button.variant (SSH-5).

props.name: destructive
props.description: Marks an action that deletes or discards something a person may not get back (Delete, Discard, Remove member): the button keeps its variant's emphasis and takes the error role's color in it — filled in the error color, tonal in its tonal container, and the error color for the label of an elevated, outlined or text button and the edge of an outlined one (BTN-40). Use it for that kind of action alone, never for emphasis. It adds a color, not a meaning: the label still says what the button does (BTN-42). A toggle has no destructive look: ignored while toggle is true (BTN-41).

props.name: size
props.description: Visual height (32 / 40 / 56), which is also an icon-only button's width at its default width. The hit area always meets the minimum target. A design system may add values.

props.name: width
props.description: How wide an icon-only button is. default: as wide as it is high (32 / 40 / 56). narrow: its glyph with a small inset on each side (28 / 32 / 32), for a tight row of icon actions. wide: 40 / 52 / 72, for the one action of a row that should weigh more. Ignored when the button has a label, and while fullWidth is true. The hit area meets the minimum target at every width.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Makes the button take the whole width its container gives it, its content centred, at the height of its size (BTN-39): a form's only action on a narrow screen, the action at the foot of a card or a sheet. Ignored while a host lays the button out (a button group, a toolbar, or the actions of a dialog, a side sheet, a popover, a callout or an empty state), which gives it a width of its own (a button group's fullWidth for a row of them).

props.name: iconPosition
props.description: Which side of the label the icon sits on, in the reading direction. Ignored when the button has no label or no icon.

props.name: toggle
props.description: Makes the button a two-state control: activation switches selected, and assistive technology announces it as pressed or not pressed. A toggle takes no destination: href is ignored while toggle is true.

props.name: selected
props.description: Whether a toggle is on. Ignored unless toggle is true.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Prevents interaction and removes the button from the focus order — unless focusableWhenDisabled keeps it there (BTN-38). A disabled button with a destination is not a link that can be followed (BTN-25); on the web a disabled submit button sends nothing, and still stops Enter from sending its form where it is the form's default button (BTN-32).

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Keeps a disabled button in the focus order: it is drawn and exposed as disabled and refuses every activation, but a keyboard and a screen reader can still reach it, so that a person can learn why it does nothing (a tooltip, a description). For an action a person can make available — a send button while the message is empty. Ignored unless disabled is true (BTN-38).

props.name: busy
props.description: The action it started is under way: the button keeps its focus, its place in the focus order and its size, draws the loading indicator's arc in place of its label and icon, refuses every activation, and tells assistive technology through busyLabel (BTN-36, BTN-37). For a save or a send that takes a moment; it is not disabled, so focus stays where the person left it.

props.name: busyLabel
props.description: What assistive technology is told while the button is busy ("Saving"): announced once when it becomes busy and read after its name while it is. Tanrei ships no words of its own. Required while busy is true; ignored otherwise.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: an address as the platform's links take one (a URL; on the web a path or a fragment as well). Not empty, it makes the button a link and not a button: the link role, activated by pointer, touch or Enter and not by Space, opened by the platform as its own links are, and drawn exactly as the button it would otherwise be (BTN-22, BTN-23). Ignored while toggle is true: a control that holds a state is not a destination (BTN-26).

props.name: target
props.description: Where the destination opens. same: where the person is — the same tab on the web, the app's own handling of the address elsewhere. new: a new context — a new tab or window on the web, outside the current screen elsewhere — which a labelled button marks with the glyph open_in_new after its label and says through targetLabel (BTN-24). Ignored without href.

props.name: targetLabel
props.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while target is new ("opens in a new tab"). Tanrei ships no words of its own, so the product gives them in its own language, as it gives a chip its removeLabel. Required while target is new; ignored otherwise.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name, where it is more than what the button draws. Required for an icon-only button: an icon alone is not a name. Optional for a button that draws a label: left empty, the drawn text is the name; given, it is the whole name in place of the drawn text, which stays drawn — for an action repeated in every row (drawn "Reset", named "Reset: Spacing") — and it must contain the drawn text, so that a person who says what they see is heard (BTN-16). It is about this one button, so it is the instance's alone and reads no word of the product's.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Label content: the text that names the action. Leave it empty for an icon-only button.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: The icon: a glyph of the system's icon set, drawn through the platform's icon helper. With a label it sits at the side iconPosition names; without one it is the button's only content.

events.name: click
events.description: The button was activated by pointer, touch, keyboard or assistive technology. A link button emits it before its destination opens; a product that takes the navigation itself (a client-side router) cancels it (BTN-23).

events.name: change
events.description: A toggle was activated; carries the new value of selected.

behavior.text: WHEN the user activates the button by pointer, touch, Enter or Space — a link button (BTN-22) by pointer, touch or Enter — THE button SHALL emit click exactly once.
WHILE disabled is true THE button SHALL NOT emit click or change, SHALL NOT be focusable and SHALL expose the disabled state to assistive technology.

WHILE hovered, keyboard-focused or pressed THE button SHALL render its container, label, icon, outline, elevation and opacity from the component tokens of the highest-precedence active state, with precedence pressed over focused over hovered; focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT select the focused state.
behavior.verify: The default system gives the pressed and the focused state layer the same opacity, so precedence cannot be seen with it. Test under the `acme` fixture system (packages/tokens-build/test/fixtures/acme.system.json), which values hovered, focused and pressed differently.

behavior.text: WHEN the button receives keyboard focus THE button SHALL show the focus ring without animation; focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT show it.

WHERE the visual size is below the minimum target THE button SHALL extend its hit area on both axes to sys.target.touch for touch input and sys.target.pointer for fine pointers, without changing its visual size; a platform that cannot tell the input type SHALL use sys.target.touch.

WHILE disabled is true THE button SHALL render its container, label, icon, outline, elevation and opacity from the disabled component tokens of its variant and, for a toggle, of its selection, and, while destructive is true, of its destructive parts (BTN-40).
WHEN variant or size names a value that the active design system does not have THE button SHALL render with the default value's tokens, and in debug builds report the unknown value.

WHEN the button is pressed by pointer, touch, Enter or Space THE button SHALL show the pressed state without delay and SHALL keep it visible for at least sys.motion.duration.press-hold, even when the press ends sooner.

WHILE pressed THE button SHALL answer as sys.behavior.pressed-feedback names: overlay applies the pressed tokens to the whole container at once; ripple grows the pressed state layer from the point of contact (from the center for keyboard activation); dim applies the pressed opacity to the whole control and draws no state layer; none draws no answer to the press. Under ripple and dim only the container color stays with the state under the press; label, icon, outline, elevation, opacity and shape still come from the pressed tokens. Under none every part stays with the state under the press. The ripple grows over comp.button.motion.feedback-duration with motion.state-easing, fades over motion.state-duration with motion.state-easing once the press has ended and press-hold has passed, and appears whole where motion is reduced.
behavior.verify: Test under a system that sets each value; `m3-like` is ripple, `cupertino` is dim, the default is overlay.

behavior.text: THE button SHALL ease its container corners by sys.shape.corner-smoothing (0 is a quarter circle, 0.6 the iOS continuous corner; a platform with only the OS curve draws it for any amount above 0) and show its keyboard focus as sys.behavior.focus-style names (ring or glow); a platform that cannot draw a choice SHALL fall back to the first value and state that in its README. WHILE the button is an item of a connected button group THE button SHALL draw its corners and minimum width and height as the group sets them, the padding the group adds at a rounded outer end, and neither outline nor elevation ring along an edge the group joins to a neighbour under a divider, and, from a dialog, a side sheet or an image preview, its variant while none is set (DLG-20, SSH-17, IMP-8) and a side sheet's close-button variant (SSH-5), through an internal channel that is not part of its public surface (BGR-2, BGR-3, BGR-16, BGR-22, BGR-23).
behavior.verify: `cupertino` is continuous; the `acme` fixture system is glow.

behavior.text: WHILE the button has both a label and an icon THE button SHALL draw the icon at the side iconPosition names in the reading direction (leading at the start, trailing at the end, both mirrored in right-to-left layouts) and the label comp.button.container.gap.medium from it at the medium size (and the gap of its own size otherwise), with comp.button.container.padding-inline-start-with-icon.medium on the icon's side for a leading icon and comp.button.container.padding-inline-end-with-icon.medium for a trailing one, and the plain padding (comp.button.container.padding-inline-start.medium, comp.button.container.padding-inline-end.medium) on the other side, each of its own size; WHILE it has a label and no icon it SHALL use the plain padding on both sides and ignore iconPosition.
behavior.verify: Fixtures filled-leading-icon and filled-trailing-icon: the icon's side and the order of icon and label; under the default system the padding on the icon's side is 12 and on the label's side 16 at the medium size (12 and 16 at small, 16 and 24 at large: filled-leading-icon-small, filled-leading-icon-large, filled-trailing-icon-large). Test the mirroring in a right-to-left layout.

behavior.text: WHILE the button has an icon and no label THE button SHALL draw its container at the height of its size — comp.button.container.height.medium at the medium size, and the height of its own size otherwise — and at the width its width names: as wide as it is high WHILE width is default, as wide as its glyph's box (comp.button.icon.size-without-label.medium) with comp.button.container.padding-inline-narrow.medium on each side of it WHILE width is narrow, and comp.button.container.width-wide.medium wide WHILE width is wide (each of its own size), with the glyph centred, and SHALL round it by comp.button.container.shape, capped at half its shorter side, so that the default system's sys.shape.corner.full draws a circle at the default width and a capsule at the other two, and a smaller corner a rounded square or rectangle. The narrow width SHALL be the glyph and that inset twice, and nothing more: the button has no narrow width of its own to disagree with them, so a narrow button follows its glyph wherever a design system re-sizes it, and its container, state layer, ripple and outline are a capsule of that width. In the default system the inset is sys.space.space50 at every size, the least room that keeps the glyph clear of the capsule's edge; a design system that wants its narrow buttons to differ more by size gives a size a larger inset. It SHALL NOT draw an icon-only button at any other width, except to the minimum width a connected button group sets and the padding that group adds at an outer end (BTN-10). WHERE text size scales the glyph (every size follows the root font size on the web) the container SHALL grow with it and keep the proportion of its width to its height.
behavior.verify: Fixtures filled-icon-small, filled-icon and filled-icon-large: the container's width equals its height at each size, and under the default system its corners meet as a circle. Fixtures filled-icon-narrow-small, filled-icon-narrow, filled-icon-narrow-large (28, 32, 32 wide: the glyph's box of each size, 20, 24 and 24, and 4 on each side of it) and filled-icon-wide-small, filled-icon-wide, filled-icon-wide-large (40, 52, 72 wide) under the default system, each at the height of its size, the glyph centred.

behavior.text: THE button SHALL draw its icon at the icon box of its size — comp.button.icon.size.medium beside a label and comp.button.icon.size-without-label.medium alone at the medium size, and so on — with the family and fill of its selection (sys.icon.family.selected and sys.icon.fill.selected only when toggle and selected are both true; otherwise sys.icon.family.unselected and sys.icon.fill.unselected), sys.icon.weight, and an optical size clamped between sys.icon.optical-size.min and sys.icon.optical-size.max; beside a label the icon SHALL take the label color of the button's look, and alone the icon color of its look (comp.button.text.icon.color for a plain text button, comp.button.text.selected.icon.color for a text toggle that is on, and so on).
behavior.verify: Fixtures text-icon (on-surface-variant under the default system) and text-leading-icon-toggle-unselected / text-leading-icon-toggle-selected (outlined and filled glyph).

behavior.text: WHEN toggle is true and the user activates the button THE button SHALL emit click and then change with the opposite of selected, in that order (as a native checkbox does, and as CHP-11 says for a filter chip), and SHALL expose selected to assistive technology as pressed or not pressed; WHILE toggle is false THE button SHALL NOT expose a pressed state.

WHILE toggle is true THE button SHALL render its container, label, icon and outline from the selected parts of its variant when selected is true (comp.button.filled.selected.container.color, and so on) and from the unselected parts when it is false (comp.button.filled.unselected.container.color, and so on), and its elevation from its variant's own comp.button.filled.container.elevation (and so on); WHILE toggle is false it SHALL render from the variant's own parts.

WHILE the label prop is not empty THE button SHALL expose it as its accessible name, whole and alone, whether or not it draws a label; WHILE the label prop is empty and the button draws a label THE button SHALL expose the drawn label's text as its accessible name; WHILE it has an icon and no drawn label THE button SHALL keep the glyph from assistive technology, and WHILE the label prop is empty as well SHALL still render, and in debug builds report that it has no accessible name. WHILE the button draws a label and the label prop is not empty THE button SHALL draw the label exactly as it would without the prop, SHALL NOT expose the drawn text a second time beside the name, and in debug builds SHALL report a label prop that does not contain the drawn text — the two compared with white space at their ends dropped, runs of white space read as one space and letters compared without case — because a person who speaks the words they see must be heard by the control that shows them. That report SHALL be all the button does about it: it SHALL still expose the label prop, whole and alone, as the name, SHALL NOT fall back to the drawn text and SHALL NOT add the drawn text to the name, in a debug build as in any other. THE button SHALL NOT make a name of the two itself, by joining them or in any other way: the order of a phrase is the language's, and the whole name is the product's to give. A description — the platform's own, or targetLabel (BTN-24) — SHALL be read after the name and the role and SHALL NOT be exposed as a name or as part of one.
behavior.verify: Fixtures text-named (drawn "Reset", named "Reset: Spacing"), filled-leading-icon-named and outlined-link-named are drawn exactly as the same button without the label prop; assert the accessible name is the prop and that the drawn text is not exposed a second time (on the web the one native element carries aria-label; no second node holds the name). A label prop of "Spacing" on a button drawn "Reset" is reported once, and the button's accessible name is still "Spacing", in a debug build and outside one; "reset:  spacing" on a button drawn " Reset " is not. A label prop equal to the drawn text changes nothing and reports nothing.

behavior.text: IF the button has neither a label nor an icon THE button SHALL still render its container at the height of its size and as wide as it is high, and in debug builds report that it has no content.

THE button SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the button is shown THE button SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping its selection and its focus.
behavior.verify: Test with the direction set on an ancestor inside the page or the view tree, not on the root, and again changed after the first render. On the web the test is owed with the other right-to-left tests.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE button SHALL draw the glyph of its icon slot mirrored left to right exactly when the system's icon set marks that glyph's name as mirrored or the product forces mirroring for that use, and unmirrored when the product forbids it: the icon helper mirrors the glyph inside its own box, about the box's vertical centre line, changing neither its place, size, color and fill nor the order BTN-11 gives. THE button SHALL NOT mirror a glyph itself, and SHALL NOT mirror content the product gives as an image or a view of its own rather than by a glyph's name.
behavior.verify: arrow_forward, chevron_right, reply and send are marked by the default icon set; check, close, search and play_arrow are not. Test one marked and one unmarked name in right-to-left, the marked one again with mirroring forbidden and the unmarked one with it forced, and the marked one in left-to-right (never mirrored there).

behavior.text: THE button SHALL lay out its label as text of its own direction, isolated from the text around it: each takes the base direction of its first strong character, or the layout direction where it has none, so that a left-to-right word, a number with its sign or unit, a telephone number and an address keep their own order in a right-to-left layout and reorder nothing beside them; THE button SHALL still place the label and align its lines by the layout direction, not by the text's own.

WHILE the button has a label THE button SHALL ignore width: a labelled button is as wide as its content and its paddings (BTN-11). WHEN width names a value the button does not define THE button SHALL render at the default width, and in debug builds report the unknown value. THE button SHALL meet the minimum target of BTN-5 at every width by extending its hit area: a narrow button SHALL NOT be drawn wider to reach it.
behavior.verify: Fixture text-icon-narrow under the default system: 32 wide, with a hit area of at least sys.target.touch (48) across. A labelled button with width set to narrow or wide renders as filled-medium does.

behavior.text: WHILE href is not empty and toggle is false THE button SHALL be a link and not a button: it SHALL expose the link role, named as BTN-16 names a button, with no pressed state; SHALL be the platform's own link to href (the web's anchor element; SwiftUI's Link; on Compose, Flutter and React Native an element with the platform's link semantics whose address is opened by the platform's opener), so that whatever the platform gives a link — on the web its context menu, opening in a new tab or window, copying and dragging its address, and the address shown before it is followed — is the platform's, and not the button's to draw or to take over; and SHALL draw its container, label, icon, outline, elevation and opacity in every state from the same tokens as a button of its variant, size and width that has no destination, with no look of its own for a link and none for a destination already visited.
behavior.verify: Fixture filled-link is drawn exactly as a filled button with the same label and no destination, and text-icon-link as a text icon-only button with the same glyph. On the web the shadow root holds an anchor with the href; assert the role link, the accessible name, and that no aria-pressed is present.

behavior.text: WHEN the user activates a link button by pointer, touch or Enter THE button SHALL emit click exactly once and then open href where target names, unless the product cancelled that click, in which case it SHALL open nothing: the product's own router has taken the navigation. It SHALL show the pressed state as BTN-8 and BTN-9 say and SHALL NOT hold the navigation back for sys.motion.duration.press-hold. THE button SHALL NOT activate a link button on Space, which on the web scrolls the page as it does on any link, and SHALL NOT show the pressed state for it; WHERE the platform gives its links other keys or gestures (on the web a modified or a middle click that opens a new tab, on Apple platforms a long press that previews) THE button SHALL leave them to the platform.
behavior.verify: On the web: Enter follows the link and fires click once; Space fires no click and leaves the page to scroll; a click listener that calls preventDefault() keeps the page where it is; a click with the platform's new-tab modifier is not cancelled by the button.

behavior.text: WHILE the button is a link and target is new THE button SHALL open href in a new context — on the web a new tab or window that is given no handle to the page that opened it; on the other platforms outside the screen the person is on, as the platform's opener decides — and, WHILE it has a label and no icon at its trailing side, SHALL draw the glyph open_in_new of the system's icon set after the label as BTN-11 draws a trailing icon: comp.button.container.gap.medium from the label, at comp.button.icon.size.medium, with comp.button.container.padding-inline-end-with-icon.medium between it and the end edge at the medium size (and each of its own size otherwise), a leading icon keeping its own side as BTN-11 says; in the label color of its look and state; through the icon helper, which mirrors it in a right-to-left layout because the icon set marks its name; and hidden from assistive technology. WHILE the button holds the product's own icon at its trailing side, or has no label, THE button SHALL draw no mark of its own: the product has chosen what that place shows. Whether a mark is drawn or not THE button SHALL expose targetLabel as its description, read after its name and role, and WHILE targetLabel is empty SHALL still render and in debug builds report that a link that opens a new context does not say so. WHILE target is same THE button SHALL draw no mark and SHALL ignore targetLabel.
behavior.verify: Fixtures outlined-link-new (the mark after the label: 8 from it, 24 large, 12 from the end edge under the default system at the medium size), tonal-link-new-leading-icon (an icon before the label and the mark after it), text-link-new-rtl (the mark at the left, mirrored) and text-icon-link-new (icon-only: no mark, the description still exposed). A link with iconPosition trailing and an icon draws that icon and no mark.

behavior.text: WHILE href is not empty and disabled is true THE button SHALL NOT be a link that can be followed: it SHALL render as BTN-6 says, the mark of BTN-24 in the disabled label color, SHALL expose the link role with the disabled state and no destination, SHALL NOT be focusable, SHALL NOT emit click, and SHALL open nothing by any means the platform gives a link (on the web the anchor carries no href, so there is no context menu entry, no drag and no new tab for it).
behavior.verify: Fixtures filled-link-disabled and outlined-link-new-disabled. On the web the anchor has no href attribute, role link and aria-disabled true; Tab passes it.

behavior.text: WHILE toggle is true THE button SHALL ignore href, target and targetLabel and stay the toggle BTN-14 describes, and in debug builds SHALL report that a toggle cannot be a link: a control that holds a state is not a destination. WHEN target names a value the button does not define THE button SHALL behave as same, and in debug builds report the unknown value. IF href is only white space, or names a script to run rather than a place to go (the web's javascript: scheme), or cannot be read as an address by the platform, THE button SHALL be a button without a destination, and in the last two cases report it in debug builds.

WHERE the platform has a form element (the web) and WHILE type is submit, WHEN the user activates the button by any means of BTN-1 and the product has not cancelled its click THE button SHALL ask its form (BTN-29) to submit as the platform's own submit button does: after click has been emitted, exactly once for one activation, with the form's own validation run first and its failure shown by the platform and by the fields as they show it, then the form's submit event, which the product may cancel, and with the pressed button named in what is sent (BTN-31). It SHALL show the pressed state as BTN-8 and BTN-9 say and SHALL NOT hold the submission back for sys.motion.duration.press-hold. WHILE type is button, which is the default, THE button SHALL do nothing to any form, whatever it stands in.
behavior.verify: On the web: a form with a required Tanrei text field left empty and a Button of type submit — a press emits click, the field shows its missing-value error, and no submit event fires; with the field filled, one submit event fires after click. A click listener that calls preventDefault() leaves the form unsubmitted and unvalidated. A Button without type in the same form emits click and no submit. Enter and Space on the focused button do the same as a pointer press; element.click() does too.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has a form element (the web) and WHILE type is reset, WHEN the user activates the button and the product has not cancelled its click THE button SHALL ask its form (BTN-29) to reset as the platform's own reset button does: after click has been emitted, the form's reset event, which the product may cancel, and then every control of the form back at its initial value; it SHALL validate nothing, submit nothing and add nothing to any later submission.
behavior.verify: On the web: a form holding a Tanrei text field, a checkbox and a native input, each changed from its initial value — a press of a Button of type reset fires one reset event and all three hold their initial values again; a reset listener that calls preventDefault() leaves them as they were.

behavior.text: THE button's form SHALL be the one the platform gives a control at its place: the nearest form among its ancestors, or, WHILE the web's form attribute is not empty, the form of that id in the same document, and then not an ancestor; it SHALL be read when the button is activated, so that a button moved into a form, or a form attribute written later, is followed. WHERE the platform lists a form's controls (the web's form.elements) THE button SHALL be listed among them at its place in document order, whatever its type and also WHILE type is button — a link button too, since the element is one kind of control — and being listed SHALL send nothing: a Button adds to a submission only what BTN-31 says. IF type is submit or reset and the button has no form WHEN it is activated THE button SHALL emit click and do nothing more, and in debug builds report that a submit or a reset button has no form.
behavior.verify: On the web: a Button of type submit outside every form with form="checkout" submits the form of that id; inside form A with the attribute naming form B it submits B and not A; with the attribute naming no form it submits nothing and is reported at the press, once. The element's form property returns the same form the press would act on. A form that holds a text field and a Button without type lists both in form.elements, in document order, and new FormData(form) has an entry for the field alone; a Button outside the form that names it by the form attribute is listed too, after the form's own descendants or before them as its place in the document says. A Button inside another component's shadow root does not reach a form outside that root, as no control of the platform does; a Button placed as a dialog's or a side sheet's action is the product's own element in the page's tree, and does.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has a form element (the web) THE default button of a form SHALL be the first submit button among the form's controls in document order, a Button whose type is submit counted exactly as the platform's own submit button is. WHEN the person presses Enter in a field of the form that submits it implicitly — the platform's own single-line inputs; Tanrei's text field (TXI-3), number field (NMI-20), color field (CLI-19), combobox (CMB-28), one-time-code input (OTC-13) and search (SRC-13), once their own event for that key has not been cancelled; and Tanrei's checkbox, radio button and switch, which emit nothing for the key (CHK-1, RAD-1, SWT-1) — and the default button is a Button, THE button SHALL act as if it had been activated: click emitted exactly once, and then, unless the product cancelled it, the submission of BTN-27 with that button named in it (BTN-31); it SHALL NOT show the pressed state for a key pressed elsewhere and SHALL NOT take focus. WHILE the default button is disabled — a Button or the platform's own — THE form SHALL NOT be submitted by Enter in any of those controls, as the platform's own disabled default button prevents it from the platform's own inputs. WHILE the default button is the platform's own, Enter in a Tanrei control SHALL press it as Enter in the platform's own input does: its click, then the submission with its name and value. WHILE the form has no submit button of either kind THE button has no part in it: the field and the platform do as they do without one. THE button SHALL draw a form's default button no differently from any other: its emphasis is its variant's.
behavior.verify: On the web, each in a form of two fields: (1) Enter in a Tanrei text field with a Button of type submit after it — one click on the button, one submit event, the button's name and value in the data; (2) the same with a native text input; (3) the Button disabled — no click, no submit, from either field; (4) a native submit button first and a Button second — the native one is clicked and the Button is not; (5) the Button first and a native submit button second — the Button is clicked and the native one is not; (6) Enter while an input method is composing submits nothing; (7) the Tanrei field's action cancelled — no click on the button; (8) a click listener on the button that calls preventDefault() — no submit. Enter in a multi-line field is a line break in every case. (9) a native submit button alone, with a name and a value, and Enter in each Tanrei control named in the sentence — one click on that button and its pair in the data; the same button disabled — no submit from any of them. (10) a twin form whose default button is the platform's own, and the same keys in each of the platform's own controls of both forms — text-like inputs after typing, a number, a date and a time input, a range input after an arrow key, a select after choosing, a checkbox and a radio button, each with Enter alone and with Shift, Alt, Control and the command key held, and Enter kept down: in every engine the two forms hear the same events in the same order (the field's change before the button's click, the click before submit), send the same entries in the same order, and a submit listener reads the same value from the field; where this engine's own control submits nothing for a key (a select or a range input in one engine, a modifier key in others) the Button is not pressed, and Enter does not toggle a checkbox or a radio button. (11) a native input outside the form that names it by the form attribute, a form whose page stops keydown and keypress before they reach the form, and a form inside a closed shadow root press the Button as the twin's is pressed. Every Tanrei control that asks its form to submit on Enter reaches the default button through one shared primitive; a test of each is owed with it.

behavior.text: WHEN a Button submits its form (BTN-27, BTN-30) THE submission SHALL carry the pair of that button's name and value — once, at most, and only WHILE its name is not empty; an empty value is sent as an empty value — and SHALL carry nothing of any other Button; WHEN the form is submitted by other means (another button, a script's own request) it SHALL carry nothing of this one. THE submit event SHALL name as its submitter a submit button of the platform's own that holds the same name and value and lasts no longer than the event's dispatch, because the platform lets only its own buttons be a submitter: a product reads which button was pressed from that name and value, or from click, and SHALL NOT expect the submitter to be the Tanrei element. THE button SHALL NOT override where or how its form is sent: the address, the method, the encoding, the target and whether the form is validated are the form's alone.
behavior.verify: On the web, a form with two Buttons of type submit, name="intent" and the values save and publish: pressing the second yields form data whose only intent is publish, in a submit listener both through new FormData(form, event.submitter) and through event.submitter.value; form.requestSubmit() called by the page yields no intent. After the dispatch the form's elements hold no control that was not there before the press. A Button of type submit with no name adds no entry.

behavior.text: WHILE disabled is true THE button SHALL submit and reset nothing by any means — a press, a key, assistive technology or a script's click — SHALL add nothing to a submission, and SHALL still be counted as its form's default button where it is the first submit button (BTN-30), so that a form whose button is disabled is not sent by Enter behind it. WHERE the platform has a form element (the web), WHILE the button is not a link and stands in a group of controls the page has disabled as a whole (a disabled fieldset) THE button SHALL be disabled exactly as BTN-2 and BTN-6 say, whatever its type, and SHALL be enabled again at once when the group is; a link button SHALL NOT be disabled by it, as no link of the platform is.
behavior.verify: On the web: a disabled Button of type submit — element.click() fires no click and no submit; Enter in a field of its form submits nothing. A Button of each type inside <fieldset disabled> is drawn as filled-disabled, is passed by Tab and exposes the disabled state; removing the fieldset's attribute restores it within the same frame (the primitive form-disabled.ts holds the order of the two updates). A Button with href in the same fieldset is still followed.

behavior.text: WHILE toggle is true THE button SHALL ignore a type of submit or reset and stay the toggle BTN-14 describes, and in debug builds SHALL report that a toggle cannot submit or reset a form: a press that switches a state is not one that sends it. WHILE the button is a link (BTN-22) THE button SHALL ignore a type of submit or reset and stay the link, and in debug builds SHALL report that a link cannot submit or reset a form: it goes somewhere, and what a form sends on the way is the form's own action. WHEN type names a value the button does not define THE button SHALL behave as button and submit nothing — where the platform's own button would submit for an unknown type — and in debug builds report the unknown value. WHILE type is button THE button SHALL ignore the web's form, name and value without a report: they do no harm on a button that sends nothing.
behavior.verify: On the web: a Button with toggle and type="submit" in a form — a press switches selected, fires change and no submit, and is reported once; a Button with href and type="submit" — the anchor is followed, nothing is submitted, reported once; type="send" — click and no submit, reported once; type="button" with name and value — no report, and no entry in a submission another button makes.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has no form element (SwiftUI, Compose, Flutter, React Native) THE button SHALL have no type, no form and no name and value to send: there a product calls one function of its own from the button's click and from a field's action (TXI-3), and nothing of Tanrei's joins the two or decides which button a key in a field presses.
behavior.verify: Nothing to test on those platforms: the four notes of the platforms block say which idiom of the platform a product uses for a key that presses a view's main button, and that it is the app's own.

behavior.text: WHILE busy is true THE button SHALL draw its container, outline, elevation and opacity from its enabled tokens (of its variant and, for a toggle, of its selection, or of its destructive parts, BTN-40), SHALL keep its label and icon in place without drawing them so that its width and height do not change, and SHALL draw at the centre of the container the loading indicator's arc (LDG-1; under reduced motion LDG-4's whole circle, its opacity easing once per cycle) in a box of the button's icon size (icon.size-without-label where it is icon-only), comp.button.busy.indicator.thickness thick, in the label color of its variant (the icon color where it is icon-only), turning once per comp.button.motion.busy-cycle-duration. It SHALL show neither the hovered nor the pressed state, and SHALL show the focused one. WHEN busy becomes false THE button SHALL draw its label and icon again at once, without a motion.
behavior.verify: Fixtures filled-busy and text-icon-busy: the arc at the centre, the button as wide and as high as filled-medium and text-icon.

behavior.text: WHILE busy is true THE button SHALL keep its focus and its place in the focus order, SHALL NOT emit click or change, and SHALL submit, reset and open nothing by any means (a press, a key, assistive technology or a script's click); where it is its form's default button it SHALL stop Enter in a field of the form from submitting it, as a disabled default button does (BTN-30, BTN-32), so that a form is not sent twice. It SHALL expose to assistive technology that it cannot be activated now (on the web aria-disabled) and busyLabel as its description, read after its name, and WHEN busy becomes true SHALL have busyLabel announced once, politely, without moving focus; nothing SHALL be announced when it ends, because what the action did is the product's to say. WHILE busy is true and busyLabel is empty THE button SHALL still render and in debug builds report that a busy button does not say so.
behavior.verify: On the web: a busy Button of type submit — a click, Enter, Space and element.click() emit no click and send nothing; Enter in a field of its form sends nothing; Tab still stops on it, and setting busy while it holds focus leaves focus on it; its live region says busyLabel once.

behavior.text: WHILE disabled is true and focusableWhenDisabled is true THE button SHALL be drawn as BTN-6 says and refuse every activation as BTN-2, BTN-25 and BTN-32 say, but SHALL stay in the focus order, take focus from the keyboard and from a pointer, keep focus when it becomes disabled, show its focus indicator, and expose the disabled state to assistive technology while staying focusable (on the web aria-disabled, not the platform's disabled state), so that a person can reach it and learn why it does nothing. It SHALL show neither the hovered nor the pressed state. A link button so disabled is the disabled link of BTN-25, reachable by Tab. WHERE the platform disables a group of controls as a whole (a disabled fieldset on the web) THE button SHALL leave the focus order with the group, whatever focusableWhenDisabled says, as the platform's own controls do. WHILE focusableWhenDisabled is false, disabled keeps its meaning (BTN-2).
behavior.verify: The fixture filled-disabled-focusable is drawn exactly as filled-disabled. On the web Tab stops on it, Enter, Space and a click emit nothing, it carries aria-disabled and not the disabled state of the native button, and disabling it while it holds focus leaves focus on it.

behavior.text: WHILE fullWidth is true and no host lays the button out THE button SHALL take the whole inline size its container gives it, and SHALL keep the height, the paddings, the corners, the outline and the minimum target of its size, variant and state, centring its content in that width — the label and the icon as one row, in the order and at the gap BTN-11 gives them, or an icon-only button's glyph, whatever width says. WHERE that width is narrower than the label THE button SHALL wrap the label, its lines centred, rather than truncate it or draw past its container. WHILE a host lays the button out (a button group, a toolbar, or the actions of a dialog, a side sheet, a popover, a callout or an empty state) THE button SHALL take the width that host gives it and ignore fullWidth: the host's own full width (BGR-17) is how a row of buttons shares one width.
behavior.verify: The fixture full-width is as wide as its 320-wide stage, 40 high, its label centred; full-width-leading-icon centres its icon and label as one row. A full-width Button inside a standard button group is laid out as the same Button without fullWidth.

behavior.text: WHILE destructive is true and toggle is false THE button SHALL render its container, label, icon and outline from the destructive parts of its variant (comp.button.filled.destructive.container.color, and so on for each variant), in each state from the destructive parts of that state, and its elevation, shape and opacity as it would without destructive; WHILE destructive is false it SHALL render from the variant's own parts. In every shipped system the destructive parts are the error color role at the variant's emphasis — filled: the error color with the on-error color on it; tonal: the error container with the on-error-container color on it; elevated, outlined and text: the variant's own container with the label and the icon in the error color, and an outlined button's edge in it too — and disabled they are those of the variant's plain disabled look, so that a disabled destructive button looks like any disabled button of its variant. A link button (BTN-22) and an icon-only button take destructive as a labelled button does.
behavior.verify: Under the default system: filled-destructive is error with an on-error label; tonal-destructive error-container with on-error-container; elevated-destructive, outlined-destructive and text-destructive keep their variant's container with an error label, outlined-destructive with an error edge; text-icon-destructive draws its glyph in error. filled-destructive-disabled and outlined-destructive-disabled render exactly as filled-disabled and an outlined disabled button. Hovered, pressed and keyboard-focused, outlined-destructive renders from that state's destructive parts, each unlike its rest. An outlined destructive link is drawn as outlined-destructive, and a destructive action without a variant in a dialog as a tonal destructive one.

behavior.text: WHILE toggle is true THE button SHALL ignore destructive and render as BTN-15 says, and in debug builds SHALL report that a toggle has no destructive look: a control that switches a state on and off does not delete anything by being pressed.
behavior.verify: A toggle with destructive true renders as the same toggle without it, selected and unselected, and a debug build reports it once.

behavior.text: THE button SHALL NOT make color the only sign that its action is destructive: WHILE destructive is true it SHALL keep its role, its accessible name, its states and its keyboard behaviour exactly as they are without it, and SHALL expose nothing more to assistive technology on the web, where no role or state says it; WHERE the platform has a destructive role of its own (SwiftUI's ButtonRole.destructive) THE button SHALL be given that role. Its label, or its label prop on an icon-only button, says what it destroys.
behavior.verify: The accessibility tree of filled-destructive equals that of filled-medium with the same label: the button role, the same name, no description and no extra state.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the button — also to a busy one, and to a disabled one while focusableWhenDisabled is true.
Activates the button; a toggle switches selected. A link button is activated by Enter alone: Space does what it does on any link (on the web it scrolls the page).

keyboard.keys: Enter in a field of the same form
keyboard.action: On the web, presses the form's default button — its first submit button — where that is a Button of type submit, and so submits the form; nothing while that button is disabled (BTN-30). Enter in a Tanrei field, checkbox, radio button or switch does the same where the default button is the platform's own.

accessibility.labeling: A button that draws a label is named by that text, unless label is given: then label is the whole name, in place of the drawn text, and it must contain the drawn text (BTN-16). An icon-only button is named by label, which is required; its glyph is decorative to assistive technology. A tooltip may show the same text to sighted pointer users, but it never replaces label. A link button is named in the same way; its name should say where it goes. While target is new, targetLabel is its description ("opens in a new tab"), and the mark is decorative. A description is read after the name and is never the name: what tells one button from its neighbours belongs in the name, and what happens next belongs in the description.
notes: A toggle is a button with an on/off state (aria-pressed on the web, the selected trait on Apple platforms, a toggleable state on Android), not a checkbox or a switch; its name does not change with its state.
Text must remain readable at 200% text size: the container grows, the label never truncates by default.

Container heights are minimums: at larger text sizes the container grows in both axes. An icon-only button's glyph is not text, at any of its three widths: where sizes are points or dp (SwiftUI, Compose, Flutter, React Native), text size leaves its circle and its glyph as they are; on the web every Tanrei size follows the root font size (rem), so at 200% text size the circle and its glyph grow together and stay round and whole (BTN-12). Either way its label is still announced.

The icon's side follows the reading direction: leading is the start (left in left-to-right, right in right-to-left). A glyph whose name the system's icon set marks as mirrored (arrow_forward, chevron_right, reply) is mirrored in a right-to-left layout by the icon helper, not by the button, and the product can force or forbid that for one use (BTN-19).

How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system (a state-layer mix in Tanrei, possibly explicit colors, a dim, or no hover at all elsewhere). Components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.
A narrow icon-only button is drawn narrower than the minimum target; its hit area is not (BTN-21). Leave room for the target beside it, or put narrow buttons in a toolbar or a group that spaces them.

The outline of an outlined button is the hairline of the default system (the divider's color), which is far below 3:1 against the surface. That is within WCAG 1.4.11: the edge is not what identifies the control. Its label is text held to 4.5:1 and its icon to the same ratio, a toggle that is on is shown by its fill, and focus by the focus ring. A product whose outlined buttons must show a 3:1 edge sets comp.button.outlined.outline.color to sys.color.outline in a layer.

A button with a destination is a link: the link role, the platform's own link, Enter and not Space. It is not a button that navigates from a click handler: on the web such a button has no address to copy, cannot be opened in a new tab and is announced as something that acts on the page. The look does not say which of the two it is, and need not: sighted people tell a destination from an action by its label, as they do in a toolbar.

Tanrei draws no visited state for a link button: it is a control whose color says its emphasis and its state, and the web restricts what a visited link may change to colors a page cannot read back. Visited links are a matter for links in running text.

A link that opens a new context says so twice: the open_in_new mark for people who see it, and targetLabel for people who do not (WCAG 1.1.1: the mark carries information, so it needs a text alternative; technique G201 advises warning before a new window). The words are the product's.

An action repeated in every row of a list or a table is drawn with one word and named for its row: label is the whole name ("Reset: Spacing"), opening with the drawn word where the language allows. Six buttons that are all named "Reset" cannot be told apart in the list of controls a screen reader offers, and a description does not appear there. The name must contain the drawn text (WCAG 2.5.3, label in name): a person who uses speech input says the word on the button. A debug build reports a name that does not; it never repairs one, because joining two texts into a phrase is a decision about a language, and the words are the product's.

On the web a Button of type submit or reset is its form's button as the platform's own is: the form validates, fires its submit or reset event, and the pressed button's name and value are sent with it. Enter in a field presses the form's first submit button, and a disabled one stops it. The default type is button, not the platform's submit: a button put in a form for another purpose must never send it by accident (BTN-27, BTN-33).

A button can keep a form from being sent twice: while busy it is shown and focusable but refuses every press, emits no click and therefore submits nothing (BTN-27 follows click), and it stops Enter in a field as a disabled default button does (BTN-37, BTN-32). Prefer it to disabling the button while the first submission is on its way: a disabled button drops the person's focus, and says nothing of why.

Where script does not run, or before the element is defined, a web Button is its text and nothing else, and submits nothing; so is every Tanrei field, so a form made of them cannot be filled either. A form that must be sent without script is made of the platform's own controls, with the platform's own submit button.
The native platforms have no form element, and the Button has no type there (BTN-34): which button the Return key presses is the app's to say, in the platform's idiom.

A disabled button leaves the focus order, so a keyboard or screen-reader user may never learn it is there or why it does nothing. Where a person can make the action available (fill in the message, choose a file), keep it reachable with focusableWhenDisabled and say why in a tooltip or a description; where the action simply does not apply, leave it out of the focus order (BTN-38).

destructive adds a color, never a meaning (WCAG 1.4.1, use of color): the error color tells people who see it that the action deletes or discards something, and nothing tells a screen reader user so but the label. So the label names the action and what it acts on ("Delete project", not "OK"), and a dialog that confirms it says what will be lost in its headline and supporting text. The web has no role or state for a destructive action, so none is invented; SwiftUI's destructive role is given where it exists, and the platform decides what it does with it.
Disabled, a destructive button looks like any disabled button of its variant: the error color is a warning about what a press would do, and a button that cannot be pressed does nothing.

web.name: tanrei-button
web.notes: The label is the default slot and the icon the `icon` slot (a glyph of the icon font); an icon-only button is one whose default slot is empty. `iconPosition` is reflected as the `icon-position` attribute. `label` sets `aria-label` on the inner `<button>` (or the anchor) whenever it is not empty; with a label in the default slot the slot's text stays drawn and the attribute replaces it as the name (BTN-16), and a debug build compares the two. A toggle sets `aria-pressed` on the inner `<button>`, switches its own `selected` and fires `change`, as a native checkbox does. `width` is the `width` attribute (`default`, `narrow`, `wide`); it does nothing while the default slot holds a label. With `href` the shadow root holds an `<a part="container">` in place of the `<button>`, with the same classes, parts and listeners. The link form: `href` is the `href` attribute; `target` is the `target` attribute with the values `same` and `new` (the HTML spellings `_self` and `_blank` are read as those two; anything else is `same` and reported); `targetLabel` is the `target-label` attribute. Web-only, forwarded to the anchor and to nothing else: `rel` (to which `new` adds `noopener`) and `download`. Cancelling `click` (`preventDefault()`) cancels the navigation, which is how a client-side router takes it; a modified or a middle click is the browser's. A disabled link is the anchor without `href`, with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`, as the navigation drawer's destination already is. Space is not handed to the press controller. `element.click()` follows the link. In a form: a form-associated custom element (`static formAssociated = true`), as the text field is, for its form owner and for a disabled fieldset (`formDisabledCallback` through the shared primitive; not while it is a link). Web attributes, not spec props, as a checkbox's `name` and `value` are: `type` (`button`, `submit`, `reset`; default `button`, reflected; anything else is `button` and reported), `form` (the id of a form, the platform's own attribute for a form-associated element), `name` and `value`. The element has a read-only `form` property. A press of a submit button, after its `click` has gone through the page uncancelled, appends a hidden native `<button type="submit">` with the same `name` and `value` to itself — a child in a slot it does not have, so it is drawn nowhere, naming the same form where the button names one by its `form` attribute — calls `form.requestSubmit()` with it and removes it before returning, so the form's validation, its `submit` event, `event.submitter` and `new FormData(form, event.submitter)` are the platform's, and the pair is sent at the button's own place among the form's entries, as the platform's own button's is; a reset button calls `form.reset()`. The form's default button is found by one primitive that walks `form.elements` in order and takes the first native submit button or `<tanrei-button type="submit">`: the text field, the number field, the color field, the combobox, the one-time-code input and the search call it in place of `form.requestSubmit()` after their `action` (or `submit`) event, and the selection primitive of the checkbox, the radio button and the switch calls it for Enter, and for Enter in a control of the platform's own, which knows only the platform's buttons, the browser itself is left to decide: one `keydown` listener per tree, in the capture phase (on the window for a document, on the shadow root for a form inside one), added while a form of that tree holds a Tanrei submit button, answers Enter going down in a native control of such a form — inside it, or naming it by the `form` attribute from outside — whose default button is Tanrei's by appending to that button, for the length of the key, a hidden native `<button type="submit">` in a slot the button does not have: the form's first submit button exactly when the Tanrei button is, disabled while it is, and never the default button to the primitive. The browser presses it exactly where, when and whether it would press a default button of its own — after the field has committed what was typed (`change`, then `click`, then `submit`), for the controls and the modifier keys this engine submits on and no others, never for the Enter an input method or a suggestion list took, and not at all while it is disabled, in a form of one field too. That press is stopped at the window before a listener of the page hears it (at the shadow root, for a form in a closed one) and its own submission cancelled; the hidden button is removed, and the Tanrei button's `click()` is called, which emits its `click` and submits as any press of it does. A hidden button the browser did not press is removed at the key's `keyup`, and one is appended again for each repeat of a key held down. A capture listener a page added to the window before the form's first Tanrei submit button was connected hears the stopped press, as a click on a hidden button inside the Tanrei button. `formaction`, `formmethod`, `formenctype`, `formtarget` and `formnovalidate` are not read. The inner `<button>` stays `type="button"`: it is in a shadow root, where no form can own it. `focusableWhenDisabled` is the `focusable-when-disabled` attribute and `busyLabel` the `busy-label` attribute. A disabled button that is focusable-when-disabled renders its native `<button>` without the `disabled` attribute and with `aria-disabled="true"`, and refuses the press in a listener of its own; the host's `disabled` attribute is written as for any disabled button, and a disabled fieldset still takes it out of the focus order (BTN-38). A busy button renders `aria-disabled="true"` on its native `<button>` (or anchor), keeps its label and icon laid out under `visibility: hidden`, draws the arc as an inline SVG circle, and announces `busy-label` through a visually hidden `role="status"` region emptied and set again each time it becomes busy (BTN-37). `fullWidth` is the `full-width` attribute: the host is a block-level flex box as wide as its container and the native `<button>` grows to fill it; while a host lays it out (a button group, a toolbar, the actions of a dialog, a popover, a callout, an empty state, a file picker) the element carries the custom state `placed` (`:state(placed)`), under which `full-width` does nothing (BTN-39). `destructive` is a boolean attribute; it draws, and exposes nothing more (BTN-42).

swiftui.name: TanreiButton
swiftui.notes: The title is the label and the `icon` view builder the icon; an icon-only button is the initializer that takes `label:` and an icon and no title. A toggle is the initializer that takes `isSelected: Binding<Bool>`. `disabled` follows SwiftUI's `.disabled(_:)` environment. `width: TanreiButtonWidth = .default` is a parameter of the icon-only initializer alone, so a labelled button cannot be given one. Not built on this platform yet: the initializer that takes `destination: URL` in place of `action:` (there is none that takes both a destination and `isSelected`, so a toggle cannot be given one) draws the same control as a SwiftUI `Link`, so the address is opened by the environment's `openURL` — an app that routes addresses itself provides an `OpenURLAction`, which is how the navigation is cancelled — and VoiceOver reads the link trait. `target: TanreiLinkTarget = .same` and `targetLabel` (the accessibility hint) are parameters of that initializer alone. Not built on this platform yet: the initializers that take a title take `label: String? = nil` as well, set with `.accessibilityLabel` over the title's text. SwiftUI has no form element that sends values, so there is no `type` (BTN-34): an app that wants Return to press a view's main button gives that `TanreiButton` `.keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)`, or calls the same function from a text field's `action`. Not built on this platform yet: `busy` and `busyLabel` (BTN-36, BTN-37), and `focusableWhenDisabled` (BTN-38). Not built on this platform yet: `fullWidth` (BTN-39). Not built on this platform yet: `role: ButtonRole? = nil` on every initializer, as SwiftUI's own `Button(role:)` takes it: `.destructive` is destructive, and any other role draws as `nil` does; the role is passed on to the system, so a destructive Button in a menu, a swipe action or a confirmation dialog is treated as SwiftUI treats its own (BTN-40 to BTN-42).

compose.name: TanreiButton
compose.notes: Compose idiom is the inverse flag `enabled`. A non-null `onCheckedChange` makes it a toggle (as `IconToggleButton`), with `checked` its state; an icon-only button is the overload with an `icon` and a `contentDescription` and no text. `width: TanreiButtonWidth = TanreiButtonWidth.Default` is a parameter of the icon-only overload alone. Not built on this platform yet: the overload that takes `href: String` and no `onCheckedChange` opens the address through `LocalUriHandler.current` after `onClick`; an app that routes addresses itself provides its own `UriHandler`. Compose has no link role for a clickable element (only link annotations inside text), so the node drops `Role.Button` and carries no role, and the README says so. `target: TanreiLinkTarget = TanreiLinkTarget.Same`; `targetLabel` is appended to the node's state description. Not built on this platform yet: the overloads that take text take `contentDescription: String? = null` as well; given, the node's semantics are cleared and set again with it, because a merged node would otherwise read the text and the description both. Compose has no form element, so there is no `type` (BTN-34): an app calls the same function from `onClick` and from a text field's `action`. Not built on this platform yet: `busy` and `busyLabel` (BTN-36, BTN-37), and `focusableWhenDisabled` (BTN-38). Not built on this platform yet: `fullWidth` (BTN-39). Not built on this platform yet: `destructive: Boolean = false` on every overload; Compose has no destructive role, so it draws and adds no semantics (BTN-40 to BTN-42).

flutter.name: TanreiButton
flutter.notes: Flutter idiom: a null `onPressed` disables the button; `iconAlignment` (start / end) is Flutter's own name for the icon's side. A non-null `isSelected` makes it a toggle and `onPressed` flips it; an icon-only button is the `TanreiButton.icon` constructor, whose `semanticLabel` is required. `width` (`TanreiButtonWidth.normal`, `.narrow`, `.wide`; `default` is a reserved word in Dart) is a parameter of `TanreiButton.icon` alone. Not built on this platform yet: the `TanreiButton.link` and `TanreiButton.iconLink` constructors (`href` is a `Uri`) has `Semantics(link: true)` with the address as its `linkUrl`. The package has no plugin dependency, so the address is opened by the nearest `TanreiLinkOpener`, an inherited widget the app provides once (calling `url_launcher`, or its own router); without one the control opens nothing and reports it in debug builds. `target` is a `TanreiLinkTarget`; `targetSemanticLabel` is the semantics hint. Not built on this platform yet: the constructors that take a child label take `semanticLabel` as well, optional there, applied with the child's own semantics excluded. Flutter's `Form` validates and saves and sends nothing, and has no default button, so there is no `type` (BTN-34): an app calls the same function from `onPressed` and from a text field's `action`. Not built on this platform yet: `busy` and `busySemanticLabel` (BTN-36, BTN-37), and `focusableWhenDisabled` (BTN-38). Not built on this platform yet: `fullWidth` (BTN-39). Not built on this platform yet: `isDestructiveAction` (`bool`, default false), the name Flutter's own `CupertinoDialogAction` gives the same flag; it draws and adds no semantics (BTN-40 to BTN-42).

react-native.name: Button
react-native.notes: The label is `children` and the icon the `icon` prop; an icon-only button has no children and requires `accessibilityLabel`. A toggle has `accessibilityState.selected` and the `togglebutton` role where React Native offers it. `width` (`"default" | "narrow" | "wide"`) is the icon-only width, not a layout width; it is ignored with children. Not built on this platform yet: a Button with `href` has `accessibilityRole="link"` and opens the address with `Linking.openURL` after `onPress`, unless `onPress` called `event.preventDefault()`. `target` is `"same" | "new"`; `targetLabel` is the `accessibilityHint`. Not built on this platform yet: `accessibilityLabel` is read with children as well as without, and replaces their text as the name. React Native has no form element, so there is no `type` (BTN-34): an app calls the same function from `onPress` and from a text field's `action`. Not built on this platform yet: `busy` and `busyLabel` (BTN-36, BTN-37), and `focusableWhenDisabled` (BTN-38). Not built on this platform yet: `fullWidth` (BTN-39). Not built on this platform yet: `destructive` (`boolean`, default false), the word React Native's own `Alert` button style uses; it draws and adds no accessibility props (BTN-40 to BTN-42).
